description: Meta-analysis of 47 cohorts: hypertension raises heart failure risk (RR 1.71); RR 1.28 per 20 mmHg systolic and 1.12 per 10 mmHg diastolic; steeper risk at higher BP.
design: Systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis of cohort studies (PubMed, Embase to June 2022), random effects models
title: Blood pressure, hypertension, and the risk of heart failure: a systematic review and meta-analysis of cohort studies.

description: Lancet Series review: timelier reperfusion has lowered heart failure incidence after acute MI; RAAS inhibitors, beta blockers and MRAs reduce incident HF, but residual risk persists. Abstract only…
design: Narrative review (Lancet Series paper)
title: Prevention of heart failure after acute myocardial infarction.

description: Olmsted County case-control (962 incident HF cases, matched controls): CHD OR 3.05 and hypertension OR 1.44; each had PAR 20%; hypertension PAR 28% in women, CHD 23% in men; five factors combined 52%.
design: Population-based case-control study, incident HF cases matched to controls by age and sex, conditional logistic regression
title: Risk factors for heart failure: a population-based case-control study.

description: Prospective cohort of 3,910 post-PCI CAD patients: 12.7% developed HF over 63 months; BNP, E/e', low eGFR and AF predicted HF, ACEI/ARB was protective, beta-blockers were not; HFpEF predominated.
design: Prospective longitudinal single-centre cohort with Fine-Gray competing-risk regression (death as competing risk)
title: Incident Heart Failure in Patients With Coronary Artery Disease Undergoing Percutaneous Coronary Intervention.

description: In CHS older adults, isolated diastolic hypertension (rare, 27 of 524) carried a ~4.7-fold adjusted hazard of incident heart failure versus normal BP over 13 years; wide CI, few events.
design: Prospective population-based cohort (Cardiovascular Health Study), secondary analysis of public-use data, 13 years follow-up
title: Isolated diastolic hypertension and incident heart failure in community-dwelling older adults: Insights from the Cardiovascular Health Study.

description: Narrative review (abstract only): CAD has become the primary risk factor for incident heart failure as MI survival improves and hypertension and valvular disease decline; revascularization benefit…
design: Narrative review of epidemiology, pathophysiology and clinical trials
title: The role of coronary artery disease in heart failure.

description: UK Biobank hypertensive adults: each extra controlled risk factor cut incident HF risk ~20%; controlling ≥6 factors gave HR 0.38 vs fewest, and risk below nonhypertensive controls (HR 0.79).
design: Prospective cohort (UK Biobank) with matched nonhypertensive controls, Cox proportional hazards models
title: Degree of Joint Risk Factor Control and Incident Heart Failure in Hypertensive Patients.

description: Narrative review: hypertension raises risk of congestive heart failure; BP lowering reduces new-onset HF, with diuretics and RAS blockers superior to calcium antagonists and beta-blockers (abstract…
design: Narrative review of pathophysiology and therapy (abstract only)
title: [The progression from hypertension to congestive heart failure].

description: In 6804 post-MI patients, 23.8% without prior HF developed incident HF within 3 months; HF carried higher mortality (HR 1.76). Even with EF ≥50% and no HF at discharge, HF (11.8%) exceeded recurrent…
design: Retrospective multi-hospital electronic health record cohort with 3-month landmark analysis
title: Incident heart failure and recurrent coronary events following acute myocardial infarction.

description: Meta-analysis of 22 studies: preeclampsia was associated with a 4-fold higher risk of later heart failure (RR 4.19, 95% CI 2.09-8.38) and ~2-fold higher risk of CHD, CVD death and stroke.
design: Systematic review and random-effects meta-analysis of MEDLINE and EMBASE studies
title: Preeclampsia and Future Cardiovascular Health: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

description: In 52,447 WA patients hospitalised with AF, 3-year cumulative incidence of new HF was 11.7%; age, MI, PVD, valvular disease, CKD, COPD, hypertension, diabetes, obesity, alcohol predicted HF.
design: Retrospective population-based linked administrative data cohort (Western Australian Hospitalisation Morbidity Data Collection), 2000-2013
title: Incidence, predictors and mortality risk of new heart failure in patients hospitalised with atrial fibrillation.

description: In 6,545 ORBIT-AF patients without baseline HF, 3.6% developed HF over 2 years; permanent AF (HR 1.60) and higher resting heart rate (HR 1.07 per 5 bpm) independently predicted incident HF.
design: Prospective registry cohort (ORBIT-AF) with multivariable Cox frailty regression models
title: Predictors and Prognostic Implications of Incident Heart Failure in Patients With Prevalent Atrial Fibrillation.

description: In 34,736 women, new-onset AF raised HF risk ninefold (HR 9.03); among 1495 with AF, obesity, SBP>120, smoking and diabetes drove HF (62% PAR) and optimal control cut HR to 0.14.
design: Observational follow-up of Women's Health Study (post-RCT) cohort with time-varying Cox models
title: Modifiable Risk Factors for Incident Heart Failure in Atrial Fibrillation.

description: Linked EHR cohort (n=4116 cardiomyopathy): amyloidosis and DCM carry highest incident HF among those HF-free at diagnosis; HCM and ARVC more often develop HF after diagnosis.
design: Population-based cohort study using linked electronic health records (~9 million individuals, 2000-2018)
title: Epidemiology of cardiomyopathies and incident heart failure in a population-based cohort study.

description: In California hospital data, a VPC diagnosis was associated with ~1.8-fold adjusted hazard of incident systolic HF, rising to HR 6.5 in younger patients without CAD, hypertension, diabetes or AF.
design: Population-based retrospective cohort using California HCUP hospitalization database 2005-2009, multivariable Cox models with interaction analyses
title: Relation Between Ventricular Premature Complexes and Incident Heart Failure.

description: In the PREFER in AF registry (n=3223), permanent AF at baseline was associated with incident heart failure at 1 year versus paroxysmal AF (OR 1.80); 17% of patients progressed to more persistent AF.
design: Prospective multicentre European registry (PREFER in AF prolongation) with 1-year follow-up
title: Atrial fibrillation patterns are associated with arrhythmia progression and clinical outcomes.

description: Among 68,909 Canadians aged 65+ with new nonvalvular AF, 1-year HF hospitalization was 30.0% in women vs 25.6% in men; sex difference vanished after medication adjustment except in women 75+ (HR…
design: Retrospective cohort study using Canadian national administrative data (DAD, NPDUIS), 2010-2018
title: Nationwide Study of Sex Differences in Incident Heart Failure in Newly Diagnosed Nonvalvular Atrial Fibrillation.

description: In 3351 people with structurally normal hearts followed ~10 years, multiform PVCs on 24-h ECG predicted new-onset heart failure (adjusted HR 1.456) versus no PVC, alongside mortality and AF.
design: Retrospective analysis of a 24-hour ECG monitoring database with long-term follow-up; Kaplan-Meier and multivariate Cox models
title: Long-term outcome of multiform premature ventricular complexes in structurally normal heart.

description: Swedish register cohort of 8,679 myocarditis patients vs 16,622 controls: HF/DCM developed in 6.4% within 1 year (12.2% if ≥50y vs 3.1% if <50y); incidence of myocarditis rose 6.3 to 8.6/100,000.
design: Population-based register cohort (National Patient and Cause of Death Registers) with matched reference population and hospital record validation substudy
title: Trends in myocarditis incidence, complications and mortality in Sweden from 2000 to 2014.

description: In 20,590 CHS/ARIC adults, any PVC on baseline ECG raised adjusted incident HF risk (HR 1.43); risk was highest for epicardial (HR 2.98) and left ventricular (HR 1.59) PVC origin.
design: Pooled analysis of two population-based prospective cohorts (CHS and ARIC) with PVC location assessed from baseline 12-lead ECG
title: Premature Ventricular Contraction Location and Incident Heart Failure.

description: Retrospective TriNetX cohort of 718,365 COVID-19 patients: new-onset myocarditis (5.0%) and pericarditis (1.5%) raised 6-month mortality; incident heart failure was an outcome but no figure is given…
design: Retrospective cohort study using electronic medical records from a global federated network, with 1:1 propensity score matching
title: Prevalence and clinical outcomes of myocarditis and pericarditis in 718,365 COVID-19 patients.

description: Narrative review: diabetes raises new-onset HF risk (pooled RR 2.14 across 69 studies; HbA1c +1% ups HF risk 30% in T1DM, 8% in T2DM); HF also causes new T2DM; SGLT2i prevent both.
design: Narrative review of epidemiology, pathogenesis and prevention of heart failure in diabetes and of cardiogenic diabetes
title: Diabetes Mellitus and Heart Failure.

description: UK Biobank cohort (n=388,827): HF risk rose with number of metabolic syndrome components (adj HR 1.54 for 1 to 2.62 for 5); raised BP strongest, high triglycerides inversely associated; stronger in…
design: Population-based prospective cohort study (UK Biobank), Cox proportional hazards models
title: Metabolic syndrome and the risk of incident heart failure: a prospective cohort study.

description: Pooled 10 US cohorts (n=190,672 exams): higher BMI raised lifetime CVD risk, with the strongest association for incident heart failure among CVD subtypes; overweight/obese lived more years with CVD.
design: Pooled individual-level analysis of 10 large US prospective cohorts with modified Kaplan-Meier lifetime risk, competing-risk Cox models and Irwin restricted mean
title: Association of Body Mass Index With Lifetime Risk of Cardiovascular Disease and Compression of Morbidity.

description: AHA/HFSA scientific statement: type 2 diabetes is a risk factor for incident heart failure and worsens outcomes in established HF; abstract gives no quantitative estimates.
design: Scientific statement (narrative expert review)
title: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus and Heart Failure: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association and the Heart Failure Society of America: This statement does not represent an update of the 2017 ACC/AHA/HFSA heart failure guideline update.

description: Narrative review arguing obesity causes a distinct 'obesity cardiomyopathy' with LV dysfunction independent of hypertension and CAD, raising heart failure risk, esp. preserved EF; reviews mechanisms…
design: Narrative review of epidemiological, clinical and experimental evidence
title: Obesity cardiomyopathy: evidence, mechanisms, and therapeutic implications.

description: In 76,822 Kailuan adults, high-stable and high-increasing Chinese visceral adiposity index trajectories (2006-2012) predicted incident HF vs low-stable (HR 2.01 and 2.43), strongest in <60y and…
design: Prospective cohort study (Kailuan) with latent mixture trajectory modelling and Cox regression
title: Prospective associations between the trajectory of the Chinese visceral adiposity index and risk of new-onset heart failure.

description: In 4653 non-diabetic patients with established CVD (UCC-SMART), MetS (HR 1.32), HOMA-IR and waist circumference independently predicted incident HF hospitalization over 8 years.
design: Prospective cohort (UCC-SMART) with Cox proportional hazards models
title: Metabolic syndrome and risk of incident heart failure in non-diabetic patients with established cardiovascular disease.

description: Mendelian randomization using FTO rs9939609 in 36 cohorts: BMI causally raises incident heart failure (IV HR 1.19 per BMI unit), T2D, dyslipidemia, hypertension, metabolic syndrome and liver enzymes.
design: Mendelian randomization meta-analysis of 36 cross-sectional and longitudinal population cohorts (ENGAGE consortium)
title: The role of adiposity in cardiometabolic traits: a Mendelian randomization analysis.

description: In 12,606 ARIC adults without diabetes, HOMA-IR >=2.5 was not independently linked to incident HF (HR 1.08); risk rose nonlinearly between HOMA-IR ~1.0 and ~2.25 and plateaued beyond.
design: Prospective community-based cohort (ARIC), median 20.6 years follow-up, Cox models with restricted cubic splines
title: Insulin resistance and incident heart failure the ARIC study (Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities).

description: In 4425 older CHS adults free of HF, MI and treated diabetes, fasting insulin predicted incident HF (HR 1.10 per SD), also without antecedent MI; echo parameters only modestly attenuated it.
design: Prospective population-based cohort (Cardiovascular Health Study), Cox proportional hazards models
title: Insulin resistance and risk of incident heart failure: Cardiovascular Health Study.

description: In 2740 Strong Heart Study American Indians free of CVD, diabetes predicted 12-year incident HF (adjusted HR 2.45; 1.50 with MI as competing risk), independent of hypertension, obesity and MI.
design: Population-based prospective cohort (Strong Heart Study), Cox regression with MI as competing risk event
title: Diabetes and incident heart failure in hypertensive and normotensive participants of the Strong Heart Study.

description: In 2391 postmenopausal women with coronary disease (HERS), diabetes was the strongest predictor of incident heart failure (aHR 3.1); 9 predictors identified; estrogen/progestin had no effect.
design: Prospective cohort analysis of HERS randomized trial plus open-label follow-up (HERS II)
title: Predictors of heart failure among women with coronary disease.

description: Pooled 4 cohorts (n=22,681): BMI and HOMA-IR predicted incident HFpEF more strongly than HFrEF (BMI HR 1.34 vs 1.18; HOMA-IR 1.20 vs 0.99), with BMI-HFpEF effect clearer in women.
design: Pooled analysis of four prospective community-based cohorts (CHS, FHS, MESA, PREVEND) using cause-specific Cox models
title: The Association of Obesity and Cardiometabolic Traits With Incident HFpEF and HFrEF.

description: UK Biobank (n=478,479): MI (men, HR 2.61) and AF (women, HR 4.10) strongest HF risk factors; hypertension and obesity top PAR; inflammatory/neutrophil degranulation proteomic pathways partly mediate…
design: Prospective population-based cohort (UK Biobank) with proteomic pathway and mediation analyses
title: Clinical and Proteomic Risk Profiles of New-Onset Heart Failure in Men and Women.

description: SomaScan proteomics in 2906 CRIC adults with CKD: 17 proteins stayed associated with incident HF after NT-proBNP adjustment; a 48-protein model (C 0.790) beat refit PCP-HF (0.693) and held in ARIC…
design: Prospective cohort proteomic analysis (CRIC derivation, ARIC external validation) with Mendelian randomization and risk-model comparison
title: Incident heart failure in chronic kidney disease: proteomics informs biology and risk stratification.

description: In 1210 general-population adults followed 16 years, longer early systolic lengthening (DESL) and DESLsystole predicted incident heart failure and MI, independent of clinical and echo parameters…
design: Prospective population-based cohort with speckle tracking echocardiography, median 16-year follow-up
title: Duration of early systolic lengthening: prognostic potential in the general population.

description: In AGES-RS older adults, panels of 8-10 serum proteins (of 4782) predicted incident HF with C-index 0.80 (HFpEF 0.78, HFrEF 0.80), subsuming clinical risk info and improving NT-proBNP models…
design: Prospective population-based cohort (AGES-RS) with LASSO regression and bootstrap protein selection; external replication in CHS
title: Proteomic prediction of incident heart failure and its main subtypes.

description: In 5297 Malmö adults without HF, higher copeptin predicted incident HF over 11 years: HR 1.30 per SD log copeptin, top vs bottom quartile 1.63, attenuated but present after MRproANP adjustment.
design: Population-based prospective cohort (Malmö Preventive Project re-examination) with register-based outcome follow-up
title: Copeptin as a predictive marker of incident heart failure.

description: In 8,089 patients with established CVD (UCC-SMART), higher CRP independently predicted incident HF: HR 1.10 per mg/L; Q4 vs Q1 HR 2.22; similar for HFrEF and HFpEF.
design: Prospective cohort (UCC-SMART) with Cox proportional hazards models
title: C-Reactive Protein and Risk of Incident Heart Failure in Patients With Cardiovascular Disease.

description: In 410 community adults ≥65 with HF risk factors, echo markers (LAE, LVH, abnormal GLS, E/e') independently predicted new HF over ~14 months; GLS and LV mass added incremental value to clinical data.
design: Community-based prospective cohort of asymptomatic elderly with HF risk factors, echo screening and ~14-month follow-up
title: Echocardiographic screening for non-ischaemic stage B heart failure in the community.

description: In 2147 CKD adults, NT-proBNP+hsTnT (C-index 0.728) beat the ARIC HF clinical model (0.680); adding biomarkers and echo to clinical variables gave 0.765 for 10-year incident HF hospitalization.
design: Prospective multicenter cohort (CRIC) prediction analysis with Fine-Gray models and 10-fold cross-validated C-indices
title: Prediction of Incident Heart Failure in CKD: The CRIC Study.

description: Proteomic profiling of 80 proteins in two elderly Uppsala cohorts: 29 proteins linked to incident HF in discovery, 18 replicated, 9 stayed significant after risk-factor adjustment (GDF-15, TIM-1…
design: Two community-based prospective cohorts (PIVUS discovery, ULSAM replication) with proximity extension assay proteomics
title: Circulating proteins as predictors of incident heart failure in the elderly.

description: Plasma proteomics in CHS and AGES-RS (n=8599): 119 proteins associated with incident HF, 15 with HFpEF, 11 with HFrEF; 55 novel markers replicated in ARIC; MR supports 7 possibly causal proteins.
design: Plasma proteomic screen in two population-based cohorts (CHS, AGES-RS) with fixed-effects meta-analysis, external replication in ARIC, and two-sample Mendelian randomization with colocalization
title: Large-Scale Proteomic Profiling of Incident Heart Failure and Its Subtypes in Older Adults.

description: In 2103 Rotterdam Study adults free of HF, larger CT epicardial fat volume was independently associated with incident HF (HR 1.34 per SD) and with worse LV systolic function and larger LA size.
design: Prospective population-based cohort (Rotterdam Study) with linear mixed models and Cox regression
title: Epicardial Fat Volume, Cardiac Function, and Incident Heart Failure: The Rotterdam Study.

description: ARIC proteomics (4,697 aptamers): 44 eGFR/UACR-related plasma proteins associated with incident HF independent of risk factors and kidney function; 29 replicated in CRIC; mostly HFpEF.
design: Prospective longitudinal cohort (ARIC) with aptamer proteomics, external validation in CRIC, and two-sample Mendelian randomization
title: Linking Chronic Kidney Disease to Incident Heart Failure and Adverse Cardiac Remodeling Through the Plasma Proteome: The ARIC Study.

description: In ARIC elders, subtle LV systolic impairment (LVEF<60%, low longitudinal/circumferential strain) independently predicted incident HF; guideline LVEF cutoffs missed most at-risk people.
design: Prospective community-based cohort (ARIC) time-to-event analysis with validation in the Copenhagen City Heart Study
title: Association of Left Ventricular Systolic Function With Incident Heart Failure in Late Life.

description: Meta-analysis of 32 studies: LVEF<50% (HR 4.76), LV dilation (HR 3.14) and diastolic dysfunction (HR 1.48) predict incident heart failure; LV hypertrophy not significant (HR 2.85, CI 0.82-9.85).
design: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 32 studies from 11 cohorts (TTE, CMR, CCT)
title: Imaging predictors of incident heart failure: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

description: UK Biobank wrist accelerometer cohort (n=96,244): guideline-level MVPA (>=150 min/week) linked to lower incident heart failure (HR 0.65) among 697 diseases; self-reported MVPA effects smaller (HR…
design: Prospective cohort (UK Biobank), Cox proportional hazards models, phenome-wide association with FDR 1%
title: Wearable accelerometer-derived physical activity and incident disease.

description: In 2,865 older men (MrOS), central apnea index ≥5 and Cheyne-Stokes breathing, but not obstructive AHI, predicted incident/decompensated heart failure over 7.3 years (HR 1.79 and 2.23).
design: Prospective longitudinal cohort study within the Osteoporotic Fractures in Men Study with baseline polysomnography
title: Sleep-disordered Breathing and Incident Heart Failure in Older Men.

description: In 3633 African Americans in the Jackson Heart Study, current smoking was linked to incident HF hospitalization (HR 2.82), higher BNP, higher LV mass and worse strain; former smoking was not.
design: Prospective community-based cohort (Jackson Heart Study) with cross-sectional CMR and BNP analyses plus longitudinal Cox analysis
title: Cigarette Smoking and Incident Heart Failure: Insights From the Jackson Heart Study.

description: In 1873 Finnish men followed 20 years, higher VO2 max was inversely associated with incident HF (adjusted HR 0.94 per mL/kg/min); top vs bottom quartile HR 0.48; CRF added little to risk…
design: Prospective population-based cohort (Kuopio Ischaemic Heart Disease study type), mean follow-up 20.4 years
title: Cardiorespiratory fitness and risk of heart failure: a population-based follow-up study.

description: In 80,982 postmenopausal WHI women, time-varying sedentary time >9.5 h/d raised incident HF hospitalization risk (HR 1.42 minimally adjusted; 1.24 after full adjustment); sitting >8.5 h/d HR 1.54…
design: Prospective cohort analysis within the Women's Health Initiative Observational Study with time-varying exposures and Cox regression
title: Association of Sedentary Time and Incident Heart Failure Hospitalization in Postmenopausal Women.

description: In 336,939 UK Biobank adults, higher Life's Essential 8 CVH was linked to lower incident HF (high vs low CVH HR 0.458); depressive symptoms raised risk and interacted with CVH.
design: Prospective cohort study (UK Biobank), Cox proportional hazards models
title: Association of Life's Essential 8 with incidence of heart failure modified by depressive symptoms: a prospective cohort study from UK Biobank.

description: In a Swedish population cohort of 5990 women, snoring plus excessive daytime sleepiness predicted incident heart failure: adjusted HR 2.2 (1.1-4.4); 5.3% vs 0.9% developed HF.
design: Population-based prospective cohort (Sleep and Health in Women, SHE) with register-linked follow-up
title: Increased risk of heart failure in women with symptoms of sleep-disordered breathing.

description: In SHHS and MrOS cohorts, sleep apnea-specific hypoxic burden predicted incident HF in men (adjusted HR ~1.2 per SD) while AHI did not; no significant association in women.
design: Two prospective cohort studies (Sleep Heart Health Study and MrOS Sleep) analysed with Cox models
title: The Sleep Apnea-Specific Hypoxic Burden Predicts Incident Heart Failure.

description: In 12,761 US adults followed 16 years, more insomnia symptoms were associated with higher incident HF hazard (HR 1.22 for one to 1.80 for four symptoms); each symptom alone also raised risk.
design: Population-based prospective cohort (Health and Retirement Study) with marginal structural discrete-time survival analysis
title: Insomnia symptoms and incident heart failure: a population-based cohort study.

description: UK Biobank (n=407,014): J-shaped total alcohol-HF association, ~20% lower HF risk at <28 units/week vs never drinkers; beer raised HF risk in women (HR 1.29 at 7-13.9 units/week).
design: Population-based prospective cohort (UK Biobank), analysed retrospectively; Fine-Gray competing-risk models and restricted cubic splines
title: Alcohol consumption and incident heart failure in men and women.

description: Two-sample Mendelian randomization: genetically predicted OSA raises heart failure risk (OR 1.26), persisting after adjusting BMI, smoking, drinking, education (OR 1.13); ApoB mediates 9%.
design: Two-sample Mendelian randomization (univariable, multivariable, mediation) using FinnGen, UK Biobank and genetic consortia data
title: Causal associations of obstructive sleep apnea with cardiovascular disease: a Mendelian randomization study.

description: Swedish cohort (n=23,260, 25y follow-up): higher EAT-Lancet diet index adherence was associated with lower incident HF (HR 0.93 per 3 points); 8 plasma proteins mediated ~9.4%.
design: Prospective population-based cohort with register-based HF ascertainment and a proteomics subcohort
title: The EAT-Lancet Diet Index, Plasma Proteins, and Risk of Heart Failure in a Population-Based Cohort.

description: In PREVEND (n=6839), latent-class multimorbidity clusters predicted incident HF; the obese/physically inactive cluster had the highest risk (aHR 3.80) and relatively more HFpEF than other clusters.
design: Prospective observational population-based cohort (PREVEND) with latent class analysis of multimorbidity
title: Obesity and inactivity cluster the strongest risk factor for the development of heart failure in a population-based study.

description: UK primary-care cohort of 108,638 incident HF patients: deprived patients develop HF ~5 years younger than affluent; South Asian and black patients present 6 and 9 years younger than whites, with…
design: Population-based study using UK general practice database linked to hospitalizations (1998-2017), logistic and linear regression of risk factor trends in incident HF patients
title: Risk Factors for Heart Failure: 20-Year Population-Based Trends by Sex, Socioeconomic Status, and Ethnicity.

description: In 464,773 UK Biobank adults, social isolation (most vs least aHR 1.17) and loneliness (aHR 1.19) were independently associated with incident HF over 12.3 years, regardless of genetic risk.
design: Population-based prospective cohort study (UK Biobank) with Cox models
title: Association of Social Isolation and Loneliness With Incident Heart Failure in a Population-Based Cohort Study.

description: In 27,078 low-income SCCS adults on Medicare/Medicaid, hypertension and diabetes carried the greatest HF risk (HR ~1.7); hypertension PAR 31.8%. Smoking, BMI and inactivity mattered mainly in white…
design: Prospective cohort (Southern Community Cohort Study) with linkage to CMS claims
title: Race and Sex Differences in Modifiable Risk Factors and Incident Heart Failure.

description: In 28,858 EHR patients, living in a high-poverty census tract was associated with 1.80 (1.35-2.39) times higher risk of incident heart failure vs low-poverty, after adjusting for demographics and…
design: Retrospective cohort study of electronic health records, generalized linear mixed effect models
title: Neighborhood Poverty and Incident Heart Failure: an Analysis of Electronic Health Records from 2005 to 2018.

description: In 2.65M Kaiser adults, incident HF rates differed by disaggregated AANHPI group; after adjustment most Asian groups had lower risk than NH White, while NHPI and South Asian adults had higher risk.
design: Retrospective cohort using Kaiser Permanente Northern California and Hawaii electronic health records, 2012-2022, follow-up through 2023
title: Incidence of Heart Failure in Asian American, Native Hawaiian, and Other Pacific Islander Populations.

description: In 23,937 low-income, mostly Black SCCS adults, each 8-point higher CESD-10 depressive symptom score raised incident HF risk (fully adjusted HR 1.04); effect confined to non-users of antidepressants.
design: Prospective cohort (Southern Community Cohort Study) with CMS claims linkage for HF
title: Depressive Symptoms and Incident Heart Failure Risk in the Southern Community Cohort Study.

description: In 81,427 veterans, MDD raised incident HF risk in HIV- (aHR 1.21) and HIV+ (1.29) adults; HIV+ with MDD had highest risk (aHR 1.68). Antidepressant use among MDD was linked to lower HF (aHR 0.76).
design: Prospective longitudinal cohort (Veterans Aging Cohort Study) using electronic medical record ICD-9 data, Cox proportional hazards models
title: Depression and human immunodeficiency virus infection are risk factors for incident heart failure among veterans: Veterans Aging Cohort Study.

description: In CARDIA (n=5115, 20y), incident HF before 50 was nearly all in blacks (~1%) vs ~0 in whites; BP, BMI, low HDL, CKD and systolic dysfunction in young adulthood predicted HF in blacks.
design: Prospective cohort (CARDIA), Cox proportional hazards models restricted to blacks
title: Racial differences in incident heart failure among young adults.

description: UK Biobank cohort (n=437,656): highest-tertile residential green space and natural environment were linked to 12-15% lower incident heart failure risk, partly mediated by PM2.5 and physical activity.
design: Prospective cohort study using UK Biobank data, Cox models and causal mediation analysis
title: Associations of residential green space and natural environment with heart failure: the mediating effect of air pollution and physical activity.

description: In a low-income Southern US cohort, rural residence raised incident HF risk 19% after adjustment (HR 1.19); strongest in Black men, absent in White men.
design: Prospective cohort study (Southern Community Cohort Study linked to CMS claims)
title: Association of Rurality With Risk of Heart Failure.

description: Among 2.39M Medicare beneficiaries, living in highly redlined Zip-codes raised HF risk in Black beneficiaries (RR 1.08), attenuated by SDI adjustment (1.04); White beneficiaries had modestly lower…
design: Retrospective cohort of Medicare fee-for-service beneficiaries linked to Zip-code level redlining (HOLC) and Social Deprivation Index data, 2014-2019
title: Historical Redlining, Socioeconomic Distress, and Risk of Heart Failure Among Medicare Beneficiaries.

description: In 4538 older adults with isolated systolic hypertension (SHEP), baseline depression (CES-D ≥16) was associated with incident heart failure, adjusted HR 2.59, not explained by interval myocardial…
design: Secondary analysis of a randomized trial cohort (SHEP) with Cox proportional hazards regression
title: Depression and risk of heart failure among older persons with isolated systolic hypertension.

description: In 3698 older British men followed up to 18 years, low contact frequency/satisfaction and low combined social relationship scores raised incident heart failure risk; marital status and living alone…
design: Prospective population-based cohort (British Regional Heart Study), Cox proportional hazards models
title: Social relationships and the risk of incident heart failure: results from a prospective population-based study of older men.

description: UK Biobank cohort (n=432,530): long-term exposure to PM2.5, PM10, NO2, NOx raised incident HF risk; combined air pollution score showed dose-response (top quintile HR 1.31), stronger with high…
design: Prospective cohort analysis in UK Biobank, median follow-up 10.1 years
title: Joint exposure to various ambient air pollutants and incident heart failure: a prospective analysis in UK Biobank.

description: Danish register case-crossover study of 331,189 T2DM patients: short-term NSAID use associated with higher odds of first HF hospitalization (OR 1.43), strongest in age ≥80 and new NSAID users.
design: Nationwide Danish register-based case-crossover study with 28-day exposure windows
title: Heart Failure Following Anti-Inflammatory Medications in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.

description: Retrospective cohort of 1525 adults on anthracyclines: female sex was not associated with incident HF within 5 years (adjusted HR 0.87, 95% CI 0.53-1.43); age, CAD and HSCT were associated.
design: Single-center retrospective cohort study, Cox proportional hazards and competing risk models
title: Sex Differences in the Development of Anthracycline-Associated Heart Failure.

description: In a VUMC EHR cohort of 9889 RA patients and matched controls, RA raised incident HF risk 21% after adjustment; higher CRP raised and methotrexate lowered HF risk within RA.
design: Retrospective EHR cohort (matched RA vs non-autoimmune controls) plus a small prospective proteomics/cardiac MRI cohort
title: Heart Failure Risk Associated With Rheumatoid Arthritis-Related Chronic Inflammation.

description: Danish nationwide register cohort: rheumatoid arthritis raised hospitalization for incident heart failure, fully adjusted IRR 1.30 (1.17-1.45); robust across sensitivity analyses.
design: Nationwide register-based cohort study (prevalent RA cohort, Poisson regression), with inception-cohort sensitivity analysis
title: Incident Heart Failure in Patients With Rheumatoid Arthritis: A Nationwide Cohort Study.

description: Meta-analysis of 8 prospective studies (8.8M people): HIV infection associated with higher incident heart failure, pooled RR 1.80 (random) and 1.59 (fixed); stronger with CD4<200, in younger adults…
design: Systematic review and meta-analysis of prospective studies (MOOSE, PROSPERO registered)
title: Human Immunodeficiency Virus Infection and Incident Heart Failure: A Meta-Analysis of Prospective Studies.

description: In 22.4M California patients, sarcoidosis was the strongest predictor of incident heart failure (HR 11.2), AV block (HR 117.7) and VT (HR 26.1); ~22% of excess sarcoid mortality was explained by…
design: Community-based cohort study using California OSHPD administrative databases (ambulatory surgery, ED, inpatient) 2005-2015 with Social Security Death Index linkage
title: Heart Failure, Atrioventricular Block, and Ventricular Tachycardia in Sarcoidosis.

description: HIV-associated plasma proteomic signature (39 proteins + 42-protein cluster) linked to myocardial fibrosis (ECV) in SMASH; cluster predicted incident HF in MESA (aHR 1.71 per SD), not HIV-specific.
design: Discovery cross-sectional proteomic analysis (SMASH) with external validation in MESA cross-sectional (ECV) and prospective cohort (incident HF)
title: Human Immunodeficiency Virus-Associated Proteomic Signature of Myocardial Fibrosis and Incident Heart Failure.

description: Pooled 4-cohort analysis (n=26,941) using g-formula: continuous aspirin use raised 32-year heart failure risk 7% (RR 1.07); never using aspirin lowered it 6% (RR 0.94) vs natural course.
design: Patient-level pooled analysis of four prospective cohorts using the parametric g-formula with time-dependent exposure
title: Long-term aspirin use and heart failure incidence: A patient-level pooled analysis study.

description: Meta-analysis of 7 observational studies (7.5M participants): NSAID use raised incident HF risk (RR 1.17); conventional NSAIDs RR 1.35, COXIBs no significant increase (RR 1.03).
design: Systematic review and meta-analysis of observational studies, random-effects generic inverse variance
title: Nonsteroidal Anti-inflammatory Drugs and Risk of Incident Heart Failure: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Observational Studies.

description: Danish cohort (n=50,935; 2,550 incident HF): per-IQR higher 10-y road traffic noise and NO2 raised heart failure risk (IRR 1.14, 1.11 adjusted); attenuated but persistent in two-pollutant models.
design: Prospective cohort (Danish Diet, Cancer and Health) with registry linkage, Cox models with age as time scale
title: Long-Term Exposure to Road Traffic Noise and Nitrogen Dioxide and Risk of Heart Failure: A Cohort Study.

description: Japanese claims cohort of 119,535 lung cancer patients: osimertinib raised HF hospitalization risk (sHR 2.56; 2.29 after PS matching) versus other therapies; older age, prior HF, AF, hypertension…
design: Retrospective cohort study using the Medical Data Vision claims database, Fine-Gray models with propensity score matching
title: Risk of Heart Failure Hospitalization in Patients Treated With Osimertinib: A Population-Based Retrospective Cohort Study.

description: UK Biobank cohort (n=411,807): long-term PM2.5 and constituents raised incident HF risk (PM2.5 HR 1.50 per IQR); elemental carbon was the main contributor; additive interaction with HF polygenic risk.
design: Prospective cohort (UK Biobank) with Cox models, quantile-based g-computation and additive interaction analysis
title: Long-term exposure to fine particulate matter constituents, genetic susceptibility, and incident heart failure among 411 807 adults.

description: In MESA (n=6814), random survival forests with 735 variables ranked NT-proBNP, TNF-α SR, CAC, LV volumes and troponin-T as top predictors of incident HF; RF-20 C-index 0.84 at 12 years, beating…
design: Prospective population-based cohort (MESA) with random survival forest machine learning, train/test split, comparison with Cox, Lasso-Cox, AIC-Cox and published risk scores
title: Cardiovascular Event Prediction by Machine Learning: The Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis.

description: Pooled 4-cohort study (n=22,756): CV risk factors associate similarly with incident HF in men and women; clinical model C-stat 0.80 men/0.83 women; biomarkers add little (ΔC ≤0.006).
design: Pooled analysis of 4 prospective community-based cohorts (FHS, PREVEND, MESA, CHS) with Fine-Gray competing risk models
title: Sex-Specific Associations of Cardiovascular Risk Factors and Biomarkers With Incident Heart Failure.

description: PREVEND (n=8558, 25y): lifetime HF risk ~24% both sexes; HFrEF higher in men (18.1% vs 11.9%), HFpEF higher in women (11.5% vs 6.4%). Eight modifiable factors explain 46-71% of HF by PAF.
design: Community-based prospective cohort (PREVEND) with 25-year follow-up, competing-risk lifetime risk and PAF analysis
title: Sex-specific risk factors for new-onset heart failure: the PREVEND study at 25 years.

description: Adding ECG-LVH, CAC, NT-proBNP, hs-cTnT and hs-CRP to a base risk model raised the c-statistic for global CVD from 0.74 to 0.79 in MESA; for incident heart failure from 0.786 to 0.847.
design: Two prospective population-based cohorts (MESA, DHS) with >10 years follow-up; Cox models, c-statistic, NRI, IDI
title: Multimodality Strategy for Cardiovascular Risk Assessment: Performance in 2 Population-Based Cohorts.

description: In PREVEND (n=8592), women had lower risk of incident HFrEF (SHR 0.47) but higher risk of HFpEF (SHR 2.16) than men; atrial fibrillation was the only risk factor with a sex-specific effect, stronger…
design: Prospective population-based cohort (PREVEND) with competing risks analysis
title: Sex differences in new-onset heart failure.

description: NHANES 2003-2016 cross-sectional ML study in 1445 elderly diabetic hypertensive adults: XGBoost with 7 composite indices gave AUC 0.96 for HF status; BRI and PNI had top SHAP values.
design: Cross-sectional analysis of NHANES 2003-2016 with nine machine learning models and SHAP feature importance
title: Advanced prediction of heart failure risk in elderly diabetic and hypertensive patients using nine machine learning models and novel composite indices: insights from NHANES 2003-2016.

description: Pooled FHS/PREVEND/MESA cohort (n=24,675): hypertension, diabetes, smoking and prior MI carry higher relative HF risk in young than elderly adults; risk factors explain 75% vs 53% of PAR.
design: Pooled population based prospective cohort study (FHS, PREVEND, MESA) with age-stratified Cox models
title: Age dependent associations of risk factors with heart failure: pooled population based cohort study.

description: Unsupervised k-means on 77 variables in 14,840 UK Biobank hypertensives gave 3 phenotypes; the male, high-atherosclerosis cluster 2 had highest incident HF risk (adj HR 1.77) vs the female…
design: Retrospective analysis of prospectively collected UK Biobank cohort; unsupervised clustering with Cox and mediation analyses
title: Clinical Phenotypes in Hypertension: A Data-Driven Approach to Risk Stratification.

description: Pooled 6 US cohorts (n=38,028): hypertension had the top PAF for incident HF in Black adults, obesity in White adults, diabetes disproportionately in Black women; 5 risk factors cumulatively 39-52%.
design: Pooled analysis of six prospective population-based cohorts (Lifetime Risk Pooling Project) with competing-risk PAF estimation
title: Race- and Sex-Specific Population Attributable Fractions of Incident Heart Failure: A Population-Based Cohort Study From the Lifetime Risk Pooling Project.

description: Noise-adapted AI-ECG on single-lead ECG predicted new-onset HF (C 0.723 YNHHS, 0.736 UKB, 0.828 ELSA-Brasil) and added discrimination beyond PCP-HF and PREVENT.
design: Retrospective cohort in YNHHS plus prospective population cohorts (UK Biobank, ELSA-Brasil)
title: Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Prediction of Heart Failure Risk From Single-Lead Electrocardiograms.

description: PCP-HF: race- and sex-specific 10-year incident HF equations from 5 pooled US cohorts; C-statistics 0.71-0.88 in internal and external validation (JHS, PREVEND), with good calibration.
design: Pooled individual-level analysis of 5 community cohorts with random split derivation/internal validation, plus external validation in 2 cohorts
title: 10-Year Risk Equations for Incident Heart Failure in the General Population.

description: In patients with HF risk factors, abnormal GLS was the strongest independent predictor of incident HF (HR 2.92); echo reclassified 61% of intermediate ARIC-risk patients and raised C-statistic 0.78…
design: Training cohort (n=926, 7-year follow-up) and validation cohort (n=355, 10-year follow-up) with CART-derived risk stratification algorithm
title: Use of Clinical and Echocardiographic Evaluation to Assess the Risk of Heart Failure.

description: SCORE2-HF, a sex-specific competing-risk model for 10- and 30-year incident HF in Europeans over 40 without CVD, derived in 25 cohorts; external validation C-indices 0.827-0.874.
design: Individual-participant-data derivation from 25 prospective cohorts, recalibration with national statistics and linked records, and external validation in three cohorts
title: Prediction of incident heart failure in individuals without prior cardiovascular disease: the SCORE2-HF risk model.
